verdict.rationale: Firecrawl's docs have an SDK overview page offering SDKs for search, scrape, and interact "without managing raw HTTP requests." There are also language-specific SDK pages for Python (including `parse` for file uploads) and Ruby (structured JSON extraction via `scrape`), so official SDKs are first-party and documented across multiple languages. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of SDK quality, and evidence of the full language lineup beyond Python and Ruby (e.g., Node/JS).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Use an SDK to search, scrape, and interact with the web without managing raw HTTP requests.
Use `parse` to upload local files (`html`, `pdf`, `docx`, `xlsx`, etc.) directly to `/v2/parse`.
Extract structured JSON via the `scrape` endpoint by including a `json` format with a prompt and schema
